answer: Each identity registers one tundra trap line, serial-bound, locking a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it signs a log of trap-days, sable pelts, and the zephyr band. An auditor recomputes the yield from tundra sable table for those trap-days and zephyr band; a count off by 3%+, a reused serial, or one line for two keys burns it. First filing 38; the kth fake pays 38+6(k-1), 1000th 6,032, so 1,000 fakes cost 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-trap ring fails: zephyr band and trap-days are keyed to the lender, not the renter. An honest trapper pays 38 once, reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
